beats.text: When Samudra still did not appear, Rama raised his bow to dry up the sea. The waves boiled and sea creatures fled.
The ocean god rose from the waves with folded hands and begged for mercy. 'Build a bridge,' he advised. 'I will hold it.'
He told Rama that the monkey Nala, son of the divine architect Vishwakarma, could build it. Nala and Neel guided the work.
Monkeys uprooted trees and broke off whole mountain peaks and threw them into the sea.
Later tellings say each stone was marked with Rama's name, and so it floated.
Even a little squirrel rolled in the sand and shook it onto the bridge. Rama stroked its back, and the three lines on squirrels, they say, are his fingers.
In five days, the bridge to Lanka was ready, and the army crossed.
